html:
The Battle of Badr was fought on 13 March 624 near the wells of Badr in western Arabia, between the Muslims of Medina led by Muhammad and the quraysh of Mecca.

A Meccan force of about a thousand men came to protect a trade caravan and to crush the Muslims. Muhammad's army was about 300. The Muslims won, killing several Meccan leaders and taking prisoners. Muslim tradition sees this as a sign of divine help, and the victory gave the young community prestige.

The Meccans took revenge at Uhud the next year and besieged Medina in the Battle of the Trench in 627. The battle is remembered by Muslims as the first great victory of the faith.
